text:
maria: paging oncall, canaries failing on 2.1.0 deploy to prod - customers seeing 500s from inference
jamal: on it. which stack? logs?
sofia: looks like decrypt errors from runtime when reading MODEL_KEYS at startup. KMS Deny shown in logs.
maria: exact error snippet from canary pod:
```
2026-03-15T14:07:02Z ERROR: failed to load secret MODEL_KEYS: KMS.DecryptAccessDeniedException: access denied for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-rotated
at runtime/secrets.go:142
```
jamal: that KMS key was rotated earlier this morning in config-management during key-rotation job
leo: deploy-bot: 1938009999 deploy started for service=runtime image=redwood/runtime:2.1.0 canary=2
deploy-bot: canary 1 started at 2026-03-15T14:05:30Z
incident-bot: INC-20260315-42 created: high error-rate on runtime canary - paging oncall
sre-lead: tagging this as P1 until rollback/mitigation confirmed
sofia: quick check: the IAM role attached to runtime nodes has kms:Decrypt only for old key arn:.../abcd, not for new key arn:.../efgh
maria: so rotated key exists but permissions not updated in the role - that's why only new key denies
jamal: are secrets stored with key id alias or specific key ARN? config-management uses alias redwood/model-key which now points to the new key
sofia: runtime code calls KMS.Decrypt with the ciphertext, KMS checks key policy + role permissions. role lacks decrypt on new key.
leo: can we patch role to add decrypt to new key quickly?
sre-lead: patching role live is risky but acceptable for immediate mitigation. if we do, ensure least-priv.
maria: steps for mitigation (short):
- stop canary 2 (prevent further customer impact)
- roll traffic back to canary 0 / stable
- either update node IAM role to include new key decrypt OR re-associate alias back to old key (safer short term)
jamal: I can revert alias to old key quickly via config-mgmt if rotation was recent. that's the fastest rollback without touching node roles.
sofia: revert alias -> old key is reversible and low-risk. however if old key is scheduled for deletion, be careful.
maria: are there customers currently impacted? Ops metrics show 12% errors on inference endpoints in us-west-2, small but real.
leo: canary 1 had 80% failure rate, canary 0 (stable) still healthy. traffic steering happened and split sent some prod traffic to canary 1.
jamal: I'll revert alias now. doing: `aws kms update-alias --alias-name alias/redwood/model-key --target-key-id arn:aws:kms:.../abcd` (running from config-mgmt)
(maria reacts :thumbsup:)
deploy-bot: canary 1 stopped at 2026-03-15T14:12:10Z
jamal: alias revert complete. waiting TTL propagation (~30s)
sofia: redeploying a canary pod to verify decrypt now that alias points back
maria: any downstream caches or prefix KVs affected? this is just startup secret decrypt.
sofia: correct. new tokens not issued until decrypt succeeds. existing sessions still ok if running.
sofia: new canary pod logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:13:05Z INFO: secret MODEL_KEYS decrypted successfully
2026-03-15T14:13:08Z INFO: runtime started, ready
```
leo: canary health checks passing, errors falling back to baseline
sre-lead: reducing severity to P2, but keep monitor until rollback fully validated
maria: jamal, can you follow up with config-management and add a postmortem entry? we need to fix the rotation automation to update IAM role permissions or to coordinate alias flip with node role updates
jamal: filing postmortem now. I'll also schedule a short playbook change: rotation must include a role-permissions update step or a hold until nodes pick up new permission.
sofia: optional long-term: change runtime to call KMS using a grant created for the role to avoid needing key policy changes on rotation. but that's design work.
maria: customer comms - small set impacted but we should notify impacted customers in the next hour with what happened and mitigation steps. ops, can you pull list of requests that hit canary during window 14:05-14:12?
leo: pulling logs, will attach later to the incident ticket
maria: handoff: oncall to jamal for postmortem and monitoring. I (maria) will draft the customer note and sync with CS
jamal: ack. I'll also update config-management runbook to prevent automatic alias flips until roles are verified.
incident-bot: INC-20260315-42 updated: mitigation in place, monitoring
maria: quick note for runbook: if KMS.DecryptAccessDenied occurs during deploy, preferred mitigation order: 1) revert alias to previous key 2) patch role to include Decrypt for new key 3) emergency rollback of deploy if both fail
sre-lead: let's also add a check in our deploy pipeline to validate decrypt on a staging node after alias update but before canary ramp.
sofia: agreed. I can add a pre-rollout KMS sanity check to the deploy pipeline.
maria: final: canary rollback completed, no further customer impact, postmortem assigned to jamal and sofia. sending incident summary to #incidents shortly.
jamal: will include timeline, root cause (key rotation + missing role permission), mitigation (alias revert), and remediation actions (deploy pipeline KMS check, rotation-runbook change) in postmortem draft
maria: thanks all, closing thread when postmortem link published
leo: attaching request IDs: [req-8861, req-8865, req-8869]
maria: closing note: CS notified customers at 15:05 UTC, no SLA breach expected but we'll offer proactive check-ins to affected customers.
